goal: Build a small React app this weekend, something like a habit tracker with local storage
interpretation: By the end of the weekend, the learner has built and run a working habit tracker in React (Vite) that persists data to localStorage, and understands the hooks and component patterns behind it.
assumptions: The 360 minutes is video viewing time only, so the plan fits about 6 hours of videos with no time reserved for practice.
Learner is comfortable with modern JS (ES6 modules, arrow functions, destructuring, array methods) given 'JavaScript fundamentals', so these are not re-taught.
A habit tracker means adding, completing and deleting habits, with daily or streak tracking and data persisted in localStorage.
Plain JavaScript React is preferred over TypeScript since only JS fundamentals are known.
Functional components and hooks are taught, not legacy class components.

sub_topics.title: React mental model and JSX
sub_topics.why: As a backend engineer who knows JS, they need to learn the declarative UI, components, props and JSX syntax, and how these differ from DOM scripting.

sub_topics.title: Vite project setup and project structure
sub_topics.why: They know npm, so they only need Vite scaffolding, the dev server, file layout and how the entry point mounts the app.

sub_topics.title: Components, props and composition patterns
sub_topics.why: A habit tracker needs a list, items, a form and a header, so they need to split the UI into reusable components and pass data and callbacks down.

sub_topics.title: useState, event handling, controlled forms and rendering lists
sub_topics.why: Adding, toggling and deleting habits requires state updates, controlled inputs, keys and immutable updates to arrays and objects.

sub_topics.title: useEffect and persisting state to localStorage
sub_topics.why: Saving and loading habits needs side effects, dependency arrays, lazy state initialization and JSON serialization, which they already know. A custom useLocalStorage hook is a good fit.

sub_topics.title: Custom hooks, lifting state up and component patterns
sub_topics.why: Structuring the app cleanly means extracting reusable logic and deciding where state lives, a step toward maintainable code.

sub_topics.title: Build a habit tracker app in React end to end
sub_topics.why: A project video that builds a similar app with local storage ties all the concepts together and is the backbone of the plan.

picks.title: Learn React With This ONE Project
picks.reason: Project-based start: the chapters for this stretch cover project setup, a template walkthrough, JSX and components, then a movie card component with conditional rendering, map() over a list and state. That fills the learner's missing JSX, components, props and list-rendering basics with a hands-on build instead of a lecture. The movie app is not a habit tracker, so the learner should map the patterns across.

evidence.quote: In this video, you'll learn React by walking through a practical project.
We're going to use a real-world API that can fetch and display data, and cover all of the important React components and features.

picks.confidence_note: No transcript, so this rests on chapter titles. The off_topic flag (movie app) and the unverified Vite setup lower confidence. A transcript confirming Vite and props explanations would raise it.

picks.title: Build this to-do-list app with React! ☝
picks.reason: A to-do list built using only useState, with chapters for setup, HTML structure, CSS and JS functions. It gives practice on the add/complete/delete-style state logic and event handlers a habit tracker needs, and avoids useEffect so it stays on this one concept. It is closer to a habit tracker's add/delete list than the movie app.

evidence.quote: This is a project you can write using React JS with only using the useState hook.

picks.confidence_note: No transcript, so form handling and Vite use are unconfirmed. The 7-minute CSS chapter is not essential. Transcript evidence of controlled inputs would raise confidence.

It teaches how useEffect and its dependency array work and shows a controlled search input, which the learner needs before wiring effects to localStorage. picks.title: React To-Do App Part 2: Local Storage + useEffect — Save Tasks Even After Refresh!
picks.reason: Directly targets persisting a to-do task list: how useEffect works, localStorage vs sessionStorage, syncing tasks to localStorage and restoring them on refresh. That is the same persistence loop the habit tracker needs.

picks.confidence_note: Description only. It is Part 2 of a series whose Part 1 is not in the pool, so the learner may need to adapt the code to their own app. Unclear how hands-on it is.

picks.title: React.JS Interview Question:  useLocalStorage : Custom Hook
picks.reason: A short build of a reusable useLocalStorage hook combining useState, useEffect and JSON parse/stringify, loading saved data on mount. It turns the persistence logic just learned into the custom-hook pattern the habit tracker can reuse.

evidence.quote: In this video, we'll build a reusable useLocalStorage custom hook in React.js that keeps your React state synchronized with the browser's localStorage.
Load previously saved data when the component mounts

picks.confidence_note: Description only, with an interview-question style that may be terse. Lifting state up and wider component patterns are not covered here.

picks.title: Build a Complete To-Do List App with React + Vite | Dashboard, Reminders & Local Storage Tutorial
picks.reason: The closest end-to-end build in the pool: a React + Vite app with add/edit/delete/complete, form handling, a custom useLocalStorage hook and localStorage persistence. The learner can mirror it to make the habit tracker by swapping tasks for habits and adding daily or streak tracking.

evidence.quote: In this comprehensive tutorial, we'll create a feature-rich task management app with a modern dashboard, reminder notifications, and persistent storage.
Learn how to build a professional To-Do List application from scratch using React + Vite!

picks.confidence_note: Description and feature list only, so teaching depth is unverified. At 27 minutes it is a fast build, and Tailwind adds styling noise. A transcript showing step-by-step explanation would raise confidence.

warnings: No candidate had a transcript, so every pick is judged from chapters and descriptions only. Confidence is moderate to low everywhere. Check the first minutes of each video and swap it out if it does not match its description.

The curriculum uses about 153 of 360 minutes (about 42%), leaving roughly 207 minutes unused. The pool has no verified habit-tracker tutorial, and the remaining videos were TypeScript-based, outdated (Create React App), too advanced, surface-level or redundant. Padding with them would hurt the learner more than under-filling.

No video builds a habit tracker. The build_habit_tracker slot is covered only by a to-do app (X92kk5iT8CM). The learner should adapt it by adding habit-per-day completion and streak logic themselves, which the unused time can accommodate.
Lifting state up and component composition patterns are covered only indirectly, through the movie-app and to-do builds. No dedicated video was strong enough to add.

The first Tech With Tim range (6:02-40:00) is the intended source for JSX and Vite project setup. The Vite details are unconfirmed, so if the setup differs, use the first minutes of the Vite crash course (do62-z3z6FM, 02:48-06:28) for the exact npm create vite steps.

The Tech With Tim ranges deliberately skip the routing and CSS chapters (about 40:00-1:01:00). The second range includes context and API material, which can be skimmed. The learner already knows HTTP.

Neither near-duplicate cluster contributed a pick: the custom-hook pair (N7rs5F4f6FA, 1uiNxQIpcLU) was passed over for a clearer description, and the props pair (tjLXot9FsGE, zUV_f5j4NzI) was not needed because the picked project covers props. tjLXot9FsGE is also flagged wrong_language.
